extracted.intended_audience: early-career investigators preparing an NIH NIAID K01 (Mentored Research Scientist Development Award) application
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare a mentored K01 career development (PARENT K01 / PA-16-190) grant application including candidate career plan, research aims, mentor plans, human subjects protections, institutional commitment, and required SF424/PHS-398 components. This sample application demonstrates the sections and content reviewers expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity's instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample notes that 'Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically.' Applicants must use the FOA-specific instructions (e.g., page limits, forms) for PA-16-190 / PARENT K01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required SF424 R&R and PHS-398 components
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain the standard SF424 R&R and PHS-398 sections and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of Contents enumerates required components (e.g., SF 424 R&R Cover Page, Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, Research & Related Senior/Key Person, Research & Related Budget Years 1–5, Budget Justification, PHS398 Career Development Award sections such as Introduction, Candidate Information and Goals, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Training in Responsible Conduct of Research, Mentor Plans, Letters of Support, Institutional Environment, Institutional Commitment, Protection of Human Subjects, Inclusion sections, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Appendix). Each must be present and follow formatting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary / Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary/Abstract describing the candidate, career goals, proposed research, specific aims, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Project Summary includes candidate background, four training goals, description of research aims (Aim 1–3), innovation, mentors/environment, and expected outcomes. The abstract should succinctly state purpose, methods (e.g., 1H-NMR metabolomics), and anticipated contributions to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (public health relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief Project Narrative linking the proposed research to public health relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project Narrative summarizes the clinical problem (CAP in children), objectives of the cohort study, specimen collection and analysis approach, and how the work will serve as a foundation for diagnostic development. This section should be accessible to a general public-health audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear, testable Specific Aims that guide the Research Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample lists Aim 1 (characterize sources of metabolome variation), Aim 2 (compare metabolite profiles by pathogen), Aim 3 (assess antibiotic treatment impact). Aims should be focused, feasible within project period, and aligned with the career development plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy (significance, innovation, approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scientific rationale, innovation, and detailed approach including study design, methods, and statistical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Research section should justify significance (clinical problem), describe novel aspects (integration of clinical phenotype and quantitative NMR metabolomics), outline experimental methods (specimen collection, NMR, computational/statistical analyses), and address potential limitations. Include references to relevant literature and methods (e.g., Beckonert et al., computational/statistical metabolomics references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate information and goals for career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide candidate background, training history, and a specific career development plan with defined training goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample's candidate section covers education (MPH, PhD), prior research, and four training goals (didactic/experiential metabolomics, advanced statistics, biological interpretation, leadership/multicenter study skills). The plan should explain how proposed activities will fill gaps and advance independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and statements of mentor(s) and co-mentor(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include mentor and co-mentor statements describing proposed mentoring, oversight, and commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor section should detail how mentors will guide the candidate (e.g., quarterly scholarly oversight committee meetings), resources mentors provide, and evidence of mentor expertise (e.g., Samir S. Shah, Kathleen Stringer). Mentor commitment to candidate career development and time allocation should be explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support from collaborators, contributors, and consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach letters from collaborators and institutional leaders documenting specific roles, contributions, and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should describe what collaborators will provide (e.g., lab access, statistical support, sample processing) and institutional assurances (e.g., protected time, administrative support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for formal training in responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of RCR coursework, duration, mentors involved, and how training will be accomplished locally or via national workshops. This is a required K award component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and facilities & other resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional resources, cores, personnel, equipment, and environment that will support the project and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Facilities & Other Resources section in the sample details CCHMC and University of Michigan infrastructure (NMR cores, LC-MS, spectrometers, REDCap, biostatistics division, clinical research coordinators), space, equipment (Bruker IVDr 600MHz, Varian 500 NMR), and institutional programs (K club, Office for Faculty Development). Demonstrate that the environment is conducive to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment to candidate's research career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit institutional commitment statements (protected time, funding, mentorship structures) supporting the candidate's transition to independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample describes CCHMC support (internal grants, administrative support, protected research infrastructure), K club, faculty development programs, and division-level commitments (travel support, CRC availability). Letters or institutional language should confirm candidate's protected time and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects (IRB, risks, consent, confidentiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Protection of Human Subjects section addressing IRB approval, inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment, informed consent/assent, specimen collection procedures, risks, and data confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample includes IRB approval (CCHMC IRB #2014-1290), detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria for cases and controls (age 3 months–11 years, LRTI signs, radiographic infiltrate), recruitment procedures (ED and primary care clinic screening), consent/assent handling (parental permission, assent at age 11), specimen collection procedures, minimization of risks, data entry/storage in REDCap, and mitigation of confidentiality risks (secure research network, no identifiers in publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and informed consent procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how participants will be identified, screened, approached, and consented, including parental permission and child assent where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample describes CRC screening of ED chief complaints, screening at primary care clinics, timing of consent, documentation of assent for children 11 years old, and allowance to decline specimen collection. Consent forms must include HIPAA authorization when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Safety and Monitoring Plan (adverse event reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe a data safety/monitoring approach appropriate to study risk, and procedures for reporting adverse events and unanticipated problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample states that a DSMB will not monitor this minimal-risk, non-therapeutic protocol; PI and team will review unanticipated problems, report serious adverse events to the IRB within 48 hours, and cease enrollment if warranted. For higher-risk studies, a formal DSMB/monitoring plan would be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans for inclusion of women and minority participants and provide expected demographics or accrual goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample states 'No study subject will be excluded based on race/ethnicity' and provides expected demographic breakdowns based on ED/clinic populations. Applications should justify inclusion and recruitment strategies and provide expected percentages or numbers when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children
rubrics_metrics.description: For pediatric-focused research, describe inclusion of children, consent/assent process, and risk justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample explicitly states children 3 months to 11 years are the focus, that parental consent and child assent (age 11) will be obtained, and that studies are minimal risk. Justify inclusion and protections for minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report with planned/cumulative enrollment by sex, race, and ethnicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report format (OMB forms 0925-0001/0002) should be completed and included (the sample notes 'This report format should NOT be used for collecting data from study participants'). Include planned totals (e.g., 250 pneumonia cases, 125 controls) and breakdowns by race/sex/ethnicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals and select agent statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals or select agents/toxins are involved and provide IACUC approvals or select-agent compliance information when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample states 'Vertebrate animals will not be used' and 'There will be no hazardous biological agents or toxins.' If used, provide IACUC approval date, animal welfare assurance number, and select agent documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed budgets and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Research & Related Budgets for each year, a cumulative budget, and a budget justification detailing personnel, supplies, and other costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of Contents lists Research & Related Budget Year 1–5, Budget Justification, and Cumulative Budget. Budgets should align with the proposed research activities and include consortium F&A considerations when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete, relevant reference list supporting background, methods, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample includes extensive references on metabolomics methods, pediatric pneumonia epidemiology, diagnostic assays, and statistical approaches. Cite methodological and foundational literature to justify study design and analysis plans.
